title: Indicator: Force Index
description: Force Index = Volume x price change, EMA-smoothed (2-period for entry timing, 13-period for trend confirmation). Feeds Screen 2 (wave) and the volume-confirmation confidence component.

checklist.step: Confirm this uses its own EMA smoothing (ema_period param), not necessarily indicator-ema's default periods — verify against docs/Analyse.md §2/§4
Implement app/indicators/force_index.py: pure function, parameterized ema_period
Write hand-computed reference-value tests for both ema_period=2 and ema_period=13 cases
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: Implemented Force Index's EMA smoothing inline in app/indicators/force_index.py (raw.ewm(span=ema_period, adjust=False).mean()) rather than importing app.indicators.ema.ema(), and reused the same recursive/first-value-seed EMA convention indicator-ema already established (k = 2/(period+1), seeded with the first non-NaN observation). Force Index's raw series has a leading NaN (no prior close for bar 0); verified that pandas' ewm(adjust=False) correctly skips the leading NaN and seeds from the first real observation (bar 1), consistent with indicator-ema's seeding choice, rather than propagating NaN or requiring special-case handling.
decisions.rationale: indicator-ema's own implementation (app/indicators/ema.py) is accepted but its PR (#3) is not yet merged to main, so it doesn't exist on origin/main that this task branched from -- importing it would either fail or reintroduce it as an unreviewed dependency of this PR. The task board entry also declares depends_on: [] and calls out that this indicator uses its own ema_period parameter (2 for entry timing, 13 for trend confirmation) rather than indicator-ema's fixed periods (13, 26), so self-contained inline smoothing keeps this task independently mergeable in either PR order. Once indicator-ema merges, a later cleanup could refactor force_index.py to call the shared ema() helper instead of duplicating the ewm call -- deferred rather than done now, since it would create a merge-order dependency between two currently-independent PRs for no behavioral change today.
decisions.rejected: Considered importing app.indicators.ema.ema() directly for DRY-ness, and considered hand-rolling the SMA-warm-up EMA convention (the alternative rejected on indicator-ema for the same reason: no accuracy benefit at this app's data volumes, adds a second special-cased code path).

decisions.decision: Addressed all three PR #4 review findings in one pass, now that indicator-ema (PR #3) is merged and the merge-order constraint from the first decision entry no longer applies: (1) force_index now imports and delegates to app.indicators.ema.ema() instead of its own inline ewm() call, removing the duplication; (2) as a direct consequence, ema_period validation (TypeError for non-int/bool, ValueError for < 1) is now inherited from ema()'s own guard rather than re-implemented locally, so force_index no longer has a separate, weaker check; (3) the length-only alignment check (len(close) != len(volume)) was replaced with close.index.equals(volume.index), which catches both length mismatches and same-length-but-offset/reordered indices -- volume * close.diff() aligns by index label, so this is the correct alignment check, not just a length check.
decisions.rationale: Delegating to ema() is now safe and non-circular (ema.py has no dependency back on force_index.py) and directly resolves findings #2 and #3 together, since #2's fix (an int/bool guard identical to ema()'s) becomes redundant once force_index calls ema() directly -- implementing the guard twice would just be a second place for the two checks to drift out of sync. index.equals() was chosen over a manual index-label comparison (e.g. (close.index == volume.index).all()) because it also correctly handles differing index length or dtype without a separate pre-check, and because it's the same idiom pandas itself recommends for this comparison.
decisions.rejected: Considered keeping a local ema_period guard in force_index.py in addition to ema()'s (belt-and-suspenders), but rejected it as redundant dead code now that ema() unconditionally performs the same check first -- any call path reaches ema()'s guard before the raw series is even used. Considered a positional/iloc-based re-indexing fallback (e.g. volume.set_axis(close.index) after a length check) instead of rejecting misaligned input outright, but rejected it because silently re-aligning by position would mask a real caller bug (passing two Series that were never meant to line up) rather than surfacing it, which is the same reasoning the review comment itself pointed at.

comments.summary: Length-only validation (len(close) != len(volume)) doesn't catch index misalignment: volume * close.diff() aligns by pandas index label, not position, so two equal-length Series with offset/different indices silently produce a shifted, wrong result instead of raising. Verified by direct execution: offset integer indices of the same length change iloc[1] from the correct 3000.0 to 2000.0 with no error. Non-blocking -- force_index has no callers yet.

ema_period is only checked for < 1, not validated as an int. force_index(close, volume, ema_period=True) silently runs with span=1 (no smoothing), and a float period (e.g. 13.7) is likewise silently accepted -- both verified by direct execution. This is the same defect class indicator-ema (PR #3, merged to main after this branch was cut) explicitly fixed with a TypeError/bool-exclusion guard, and this PR's own decision entry cites that convention. Non-blocking -- worth applying the same guard in a follow-up.

Non-blocking, not actionable at PR-cut time: the inline ewm(span=ema_period, adjust=False).mean() duplicates what is now app.indicators.ema.ema() on main (PR #3 merged 2026-09-12T14:40:54Z, after this branch's last commit at 14:27:40Z, confirmed via git log/git show against origin/main). The task's decision record already anticipates this as a deferred follow-up once indicator-ema merges -- flagging here now that it's actionable, not as a gap in this PR.
